text:
alex_cheng: ran an nsys repro for the 2.3 perf regression — seeing a long stall around kernel launches during kv cache refill. uploading but want to confirm scrub + naming before I drop it in the bucket.

maria_gomez: upload to s3://redwood-perf-bundles/eng-runtime/… please follow the naming playbook so perf-bot can auto-index.

alex_cheng: cool, what's an example name? we have ticket RW-2431 and git sha 4f7a2b9.

maria_gomez: use: "proj-RW2431-nsys-4f7a2b9-kernel-ksel-kvcache-1792334455.tar.gz" — basically: <team>-<ticket>-<tool>-<gitsha>-<short-desc>-<thread_ts>. keep it short but searchable.

devin_kim: quick checklist for redaction: remove customer prompt payloads, replace any uuids/ids with <REDACTED_ID>, and strip full input tokens. We keep perf counters and kernel names.

alex_cheng: what's the recommended scrub command? I used the internal scrubber but want to verify flags.

maria_gomez: run the scrubber like this:
```
./tools/scrub_trace.sh --input out.nsys --strip-tokens --mask-uuids --output scrubbed-out.nsys
```
Also add a plaintext README inside the tar with: repro steps, model config (quant, seq len), batch pattern, and whether kv-cache warm/cold.

devin_kim: for kernel selection triage: look at NVTX regions + nsys kernel timeline. Check long GEMM/conv kernels and any memcpy peaks. If it's KV refill, filter on kernels labelled kv_cache_* or cache_refill.

sam_irving: small tip — annotate the trace with these runtime markers before profiling:
```
export RL_NVTX_PREFIX="KV_REFILL"
# inside runtime: nvtxMarkA("kv-cache:refill-start")
nvtxMarkA("kv-cache:refill-end")
```
That makes KV windows obvious in the timeline.

alex_cheng: good call. I also saw many 1-2ms gaps between launches — could that be batching heuristics?

devin_kim: yes — if continuous-batching threshold is too low you get more tiny launches. Inspect the request arrival histogram + batching decisions in the console for that run. Also check kernel selection logs: runtime may choose slower kernel if sequence length distribution mismatches compiled kernels.

maria_gomez: when you upload, include: scrubbed trace, raw nsys export (if policy allows), README, pipeline log snippet (with kernel-selection debug), and a short note "suspected batching/kv refill". Perf-bot will pick up and tag.

perf-bot: uploaded bundle received will be indexed in 5–10m. Use `@perf-bot triage <bundle>` to create a perf ticket. Ensure naming follows playbook or auto-index fails. :robot_face:

alex_cheng: one more — any special steps for perf regressions that look hardware-specific (e.g., new driver stack)?

sam_irving: capture `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,pstate --format=csv` and `dmesg` output. If suspect kernel launch serialization, collect per-CPU scheduling info (perf sched) too. Put these in diagnostics/ in the tar.

devin_kim: final triage steps I use: reproduce under controlled load, attach perf bundle, run small targeted microbench to isolate GEMM vs dma, and then post to eng-runtime with tag `perf:high-prio` if it impacts p95.

alex_cheng: thanks all — I'll scrub, name with the RW2431 example, upload to s3 and ping `@perf-bot triage` after. If anyone wants a look before upload ping me. :thumbsup:
